types.embedding_query_text: Event: An occurrence or happening that has a specific date and time. Also called incident, operation, strike, attack, conflict. Examples: Iranian attack on a United States military site in Jordan, US-Israel war on Iran, March 1 Iranian strikes, March refuelling crash.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The mentions describe military and geopolitical events (attacks, strikes, ceasefire breakdowns) which align with schema.org's general Event class for time-bound occurrences.

mentions: Iranian attack on a United States military site in Jordan
Controlled detonation of downed drone in Iraq
US attacks on Strait of Hormuz sites

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a common purpose or function. Also called institution, corps, command, think tank, military force. Examples: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Pentagon, Defense Priorities think tank, King’s College London.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The mentions include military organizations, government departments, and defense think tanks which fit the broad schema.org Organization class for structured groups.

mentions: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A specific geographic place or site. Also called base, installation, facility, airbase, military site. Examples: United States military site in Jordan, United States military installations in Middle East and Gulf, Tactical operations centre in Kuwait, Prince Sultan airbase in Saudi Arabia.

chosen_type.label: DefenceEstablishment
chosen_type.justification: The mentions specifically describe military sites and installations, which match the schema.org DefenceEstablishment class for government facilities used for defense.

mentions: United States military site in Jordan
United States military installations in Middle East and Gulf
Prince Sultan airbase in Saudi Arabia
Prince Hassan and King Faisal bases in Jordan

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A measurable amount or count of something. Also called number, total, casualty, toll, capacity. Examples: 18 US military deaths, 50,000 US forces, 500 US soldiers wounded, 220 damaged/destroyed structures and equipment.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are numerical measures of military casualties, personnel, and damaged assets, which align with schema.org's Quantity data type for measurable amounts.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called expert, official, analyst, military leader, scholar. Examples: Jennifer Kavanagh, Andreas Krieg, Mona Yacoubian, Jason Campbell.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are named individuals, fitting schema.org's Person class for identifying human beings.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitaryEquipment: Weapons, vehicles, or systems used for military purposes. Also called arsenal, defense system, missile, drone, interceptor. Examples: Patriot systems, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD), air defense system, surface-to-air missiles.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: MedicalDevicePurpose
candidates.comment: An enumeration of categories for medical devices, organized by their purpose or intended use. Also called device use, medical equipment function, intended purpose. Examples: "Diagnostic", "Therapeutic", "Surgical", "Monitoring".

candidates.label: TaxiStand
candidates.comment: A civic structure or designated area where taxis wait for passengers. Also called cab stand, taxi rank, hack stand. Examples: a taxi stand at an airport, a designated taxi area outside a hotel, a street corner taxi queue.

candidates.label: OfficeEquipmentStore
candidates.comment: An OfficeEquipmentStore is a local business that sells supplies and equipment for offices. Also called office supply store, stationery shop, business equipment retailer. Examples: Staples, Office Depot, a local stationery shop. Distinct from ComputerStore, which specializes in computers.
